# Autonomy Decided Before the Run

Three levels — `readonly`, `auto` (default), `full` — chosen in settings or from the panel *before* a
task starts, and passed to both executors as flags. There is no per-action approval, because there is
nowhere to put one.

## Why there is no Allow button

Both CLIs are spawned non-interactively so their output can be parsed as structured events
([[drive-the-clis-not-the-apis]]). A non-interactive process has no one to ask. Adding approval would
mean either running the CLIs interactively — giving up the structured stream that everything here
depends on — or building a proxy that intercepts tool calls, which is the agent loop this project
decided not to write.

Parallelism makes it worse rather than better: three agents in a wave produce three interleaved
prompts about work the user cannot see, which is not consent, it is a queue of guesses.

So the control that remains is **honest defaults, visible level, before the fact**:

| Level | [[claude-code-cli]] | [[codex-cli]] |
|---|---|---|
| `readonly` | `--permission-mode plan` | `sandbox_mode=read-only` |
| `auto` | `acceptEdits` + an allow-list of build/test/inspect commands | `workspace-write` |
| `full` | `bypassPermissions` | `danger-full-access` |

## The claim that is deliberately not made

The documentation states plainly that this is **not a sandbox**. The levels are the vendors' own
enforcement, and `full` is exactly what its name says. What the design does offer is one structural
property that survives even at `full`: the router — the only component that reads every subtask's
output — has no tools at all, so text that persuades it can produce a wrong answer but cannot produce
an action.

Saying "this is not a sandbox" out loud is the actual decision. A security section that oversells
what it enforces is worse than none, because it converts a user's caution into misplaced confidence.

## Rejected

**Per-action approval.** Costs the structured stream, or the whole agent loop.
**A single "yolo" boolean.** Two states cannot express "may run the test suite, may not run
anything".
**Sandboxing the CLIs here** (containers, seccomp). Out of scope for an editor extension, and a
half-sandbox invites the overclaim above.
